Title: 207 stranded as bad weather diverts China flight to Terengganu
Article:
KUALA NERUS: A total of 207 passengers and crew members of Qingdao Airlines flight QW907 from China were stranded at Sultan Mahmud Airport (LTSM) yesterday afternoon due to bad weather.
Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the Airbus A321neo aircraft was scheduled to land at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) but diverted to LTSM after circling for more than an hour in inclement weather.
He said all passengers were temporarily accommodated at three hotels in Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus while awaiting further arrangements.
"The flight landed safely at LTSM at 5.30pm yesterday after it was unable to divert to Penang International Airport due to insufficient fuel.
"As LTSM does not have refuelling facilities, fuel supplies for the aircraft would have to be arranged from either Kuantan, Pahang or Kota Baru, Kelantan," he said when contacted today. -BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 70,195 undocumented migrants detained in 10 months
Article:
PETALING JAYA: A total of 70,195 undocumented migrants were detained in 11,808 enforcement operations conducted by the Immigration Department nationwide between Jan 1 and Oct 31.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 155,498 people were inspected during the same period, while 328,744 registered under the Migrant Repatriation Programme 2.0.
Of those registered, 243,501 had returned to their home countries through the programme.
"During the same period, 52,585 undocumented migrants were deported after completing the legal and documentation processes," he said.
Zakaria said the department continued to take enforcement action against foreigners who breached immigration regulations, including overstaying, misusing passes or staying in the country without valid documents.
He said operations were targeted at high-risk areas where immigration offences were likely to occur, including residential areas, workplaces, business premises and locations frequented by foreigners.
Monitoring also focused on various methods used to breach immigration regulations, including misuse of pass facilities, the use of premises for accommodation or transit, and the illegal employment of foreigners.s
"Information gathered through surveillance and cooperation with other agencies helps the department identify those suspected of breaching immigration laws and plan enforcement operations," he said.
The department also conducted operations jointly with other enforcement agencies, including the police, National Registration Department and local authorities.S

Title: Retiree loses RM80,000 in WhatsApp investment scam
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A 63-year-old retiree lost RM80,000 after falling victim to a non-existent online investment scheme promoted through WhatsApp.
District police chief assistant commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim joined the scheme earlier this month after being introduced to it by an acquaintance.
He said the victim was lured by promises of substantial returns within a short period.
"Initially, the victim invested RM93,525 from his retirement savings and received a return of RM18,000 on Nov 11.
"Encouraged by the profit, he made three further transactions totalling RM80,000 on Nov 12. However, he did not receive any returns and was told that his investment had yet to reach the RM100,000 threshold," he said.
He said the victim realised he had been cheated when he was instructed to make an additional payment of RM50,000 to access the promised profits.
He said the victim lodged a police report at 6.20pm yesterday, adding that police were investigating the case under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
The offence carries a maximum penalty of 10 years' jail, and whipping.

Title: GKB sets record for largest number of children joining gut health programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A large number of children took part in a gut health awareness programme organised by GK Bio International Sdn Bhd (GKB), earning the company a place in the Malaysia Book of Records.
The achievement was recognised under the category 'Largest Children Participation in Gut Health Awareness Programme'.
The record was set during Zoo Builders, a five-day interactive educational event held from Nov 5 to 9 at Sunway Pyramid, Selangor.
The initiative reflects GKB's commitment to promoting preventive healthcare and encouraging healthier lifestyle habits from an early age.
HANDS-ON LEARNING
Through interactive learning stations, children were introduced to the importance of maintaining good digestive health, making balanced food choices and drinking sufficient water every day.
One of the main attractions was the Builder Base station, which served as the official participation checkpoint for the Malaysia Book of Records achievement.
At the station, children selected their usual daily water intake levels before taking part in a food selection activity. They then created their own meal plates using food props based on their eating habits.
GKB consultants introduced the Health Ministry's Suku-Suku Separuh concept, which encourages balanced meals comprising one-quarter grains or carbohydrates, one-quarter protein and half vegetables and fruits.
The children were also introduced to the Bristol Stool Chart through age-appropriate explanations. This helped them understand how stool appearance can provide useful clues about digestive health.
The activities were designed to turn health information into practical lessons that children could understand and apply in their daily lives.
Beyond the educational component, Zoo Builders featured three other activity stations.
These included Builder Supply Point, where families could explore GKB's health and wellness products; Builder Portrait, a dedicated photo area; and Builder Reward, where children who completed the activities could collect complimentary tokens and take part in lucky spin and gashapon games.
ENCOURAGING HEALTHIER HABITS
GKB said the initiative was part of its broader effort to bridge the gap between scientific health knowledge and everyday living.
The company believes that developing an understanding of gut health during childhood can help children adopt healthier habits as they grow older.
As a science-driven health and wellness company, GKB specialises in probiotics, medicinal fungi, functional ingredients and innovative health solutions.
It is supported by more than 150 research and development professionals, including food technologists, pharmacists and dietitians, and offers more than 30 product lines.
Its products are distributed through more than 3,000 retail outlets, hospitals and clinics nationwide. The company also has an expanding presence in Singapore and Brunei.
Through initiatives such as Zoo Builders, GKB aims to encourage families to take a more proactive approach to preventive healthcare.
The programme reinforces the importance of balanced nutrition, adequate hydration and everyday wellness.

Title: MBPP culls 2,782 pigeons, crows in October
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) culled 2,782 pigeons and crows last month to curb pest nuisances and maintain public hygiene.
MBPP said 1,035 pigeons were captured while 1,747 crows were culled during ongoing population control operations.
It also destroyed 36 crow nests to curb breeding and reduce safety risks, particularly in residential areas and commercial hubs.
"To deter public feeding, which contributes to population surges, we also issued seven compounds under Section 47(1)(g) of the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974," it said in a Facebook statement.
MBPP reminded the public not to feed pigeons and crows in public spaces, as this attracts flocks, accelerates breeding and causes environmental pollution through droppings and food waste.
The city council also advised residents and businesses to dispose of food waste properly and keep their surroundings clean.
A total of 14,185 crows and 12,004 pigeons were culled at identified hotspots between January and September.
In 2025, MBPP culled 17,750 crows and captured 10,171 pigeons.

Title: Rauf to be sworn in as Melaka chief minister today
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to be sworn in as chief minister today.
BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured enough seats to form the state government in yesterday's 16th Melaka state election.
The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled to take place at 11am at the Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri's office, paving the way for Rauf to continue leading the state for a second term.
The BN-PN cooperation secured 24 of the 28 state seats contested, giving it a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.
BN won 21 seats, while PN secured three.
Earlier, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced that the alliance would nominate
Ab Rauf
to continue leading the state government following its victory in the election.
Rauf secured a more
convincing victory
in defending the Tanjung Bidara seat, winning by a majority of 8,615 votes compared with just 364 votes in the 15th Melaka state election in 2021.
He defeated Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri in a straight fight.
In the 2021 state election, Rauf won Tanjung Bidara in a three-cornered contest with 3,559 votes, defeating PN candidate Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin, who received 3,195 votes, and PH candidate Zainal Hassan, who garnered 489 votes.
Rauf was appointed Melaka's 13th chief minister on March 31, 2023, replacing Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali, who resigned.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Refugees, online scams among Dewan Rakyat focus next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rohingya refugees, cybercrime, haze and public health, including youth mental health, are among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat next week.
According to the Order Paper published on Parliament's official website, Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong) will ask the Home Ministry for the latest number of Rohingya refugees in Malaysia and how many were repatriated to Myanmar this year.
He also wants the government to explain how the Rohingya refugees entered Malaysia and which agencies are responsible for the lapses that allowed their entry.
Datuk Muhammad Bakhtiar Wan Chik (PH-Balik Pulau) will ask the home minister to outline the government's long-term mechanisms for managing Rohingya refugees still in Malaysia following the suspension of third-country resettlement efforts.
This includes resettlement targets and cooperation with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and third countries.
On the same issue, Azahari Hasan (PN-Padang Rengas) will ask the home minister about the Home Ministry's monitoring and enforcement mechanisms for the Rohingya community in Malaysia to ensure refugee status is not misused to commit crimes or engage in activities that threaten public safety.
Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob (BN-Bera) will seek details on the government's long-term strategy for managing refugees and asylum seekers, as well as the extent to which the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) can ensure their identities are verified and their status, security and whereabouts in the country are monitored.
The Home Ministry will also be asked by Rushdan Rusmi (PN-Padang Besar) to provide an update on the comprehensive digital mapping of the Malaysia-Thailand border in Perlis, including the identification of illegal crossing routes, high-risk areas, security gaps and locations requiring immediate security intervention.
He also wants to know whether the government has an integrated geospatial database that can be accessed under controlled conditions.
Meanwhile, Dr Halimah Ali (PN-Kapar) will ask the home minister about measures to strengthen the police force in terms of the number and expertise of investigators, technology, digital forensics, as well as the powers and resources needed to tackle increasingly complex crimes.
These include cybercrime, financial fraud, organised crime and cases requiring digital forensic evidence.
Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan (PN-Permatang Pauh) will seek an explanation from the home minister on the causes of online scam losses reaching RM3.8 billion, the low rate of fund recovery for victims and efforts to rescue Malaysians who have fallen victim to fake job offers overseas.
Mohd Hasnizan Harun (PN-Hulu Selangor) will also ask the home minister for the number of online scam cases and losses recorded so far in 2026.
He also wants the government to outline the Home Ministry's plans to introduce liability principles that would hold banks, telecommunications companies and digital platforms accountable when weaknesses in their systems contribute to scams.
The Health Ministry will also come under scrutiny during this week's Dewan Rakyat sitting, with several questions on the country's public health challenges expected to be raised.
Datuk Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (PN-Tanjong Karang) will ask the health minister when the government plans to introduce a sustainable national health financing framework to reduce the public healthcare system's reliance on annual allocations and address rising treatment costs.

Title: Malaysian Pacific Industries set to ride Infineon's AI power semiconductor growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) is well-positioned to benefit from growing demand for advanced power semiconductor packaging, supported by the strong growth outlook of German chipmaker Infineon Technologies AG.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said MPI had invested about US$65 million in its financial year ended 2026 (FY26) to expand its artificial intelligence (AI) server-related packaging capabilities and increase production capacity for new power modules at its Carsem facility in Ipoh.
Infineon's AI data centre power revenue more than doubled to over €1.7 billion in FY26 from €700 million a year earlier, exceeding its earlier guidance of €1.5 billion.
The growth was driven by accelerating AI infrastructure investments, production capacity expansion and higher power semiconductor content per AI server.
Infineon expects its combined AI and conventional data centre power revenue to reach nearly €4 billion in FY27.
CIMB Securities said the outlook was supported by multi-year customer supply and capacity reservation arrangements, both signed and under negotiation, which could underpin more than €10 billion in potential cumulative revenue.
"We believe Infineon's strong growth trajectory is a positive read-through for MPI, which is well-positioned to benefit from rising demand for advanced power semiconductor packaging," it said in a research note.
The firm expects the new power modules to increase MPI's AI-related revenue contribution from 13 per cent in FY26 to 18 per cent in FY27 and 23 per cent in FY28.
It said MPI is also expected to ramp up production of new vertical power delivery-enabled modules in FY27, providing another growth avenue through higher packaging content value.
"Over the medium term, we expect the growing adoption of 800 volt data centre server-rack architectures to accelerate demand for wide-bandgap power solutions, particularly silicon carbide and gallium nitride, creating further opportunities for MPI to capture higher semiconductor packaging content per AI server," it said.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on MPI but lowered its target price to RM48.50 from its previous valuation.
The revised target price is based on a lower price-to-earnings multiple of 29 times, compared with 37 times previously, while rolling forward its valuation to end in 2027.
CIMB Securities said the lower valuation reflected weaker global technology sentiment amid inflationary pressures and concerns over a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure investment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Nazrin confers state honours on 218 recipients
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today graced the Pledge of Loyalty and Investiture Ceremony held in conjunction with his 70th birthday at Istana Iskandariah.
Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di-Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Sultan Idris.
Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad was also present.
Earlier, Sultan Nazrin inspected a guard of honour comprising 103 members and three officers from the Royal Army Engineers Regiment 2 Division, based at Sangro Camp, Taiping, led by Colonel Abdul Rahim Hamzah.
The guard of honour was headed by Major Mohd Izuan Mohamed, with Warrant Officer 1 Mohamad Fairus Nizam Zabory serving as parade sergeant major.
A 21-gun salute was fired by the 41st Battery of the Royal Artillery Regiment, based at Sungai Buluh Camp, Selangor, and led by Lieutenant Colonel Hafizan Mat Ghani.
Sultan Nazrin conferred state awards and medals on 218 recipients during the first ceremonial session today, while the second session will be held on Nov 21.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry secretary-general Datuk Anis Rizana Mohd Zainudin
heads the list of recipients
.
Anis Rizana, a former Customs Department director-general, will receive the Darjah Seri Paduka Mahkota Perak, which carries the title Datuk Seri.
Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman will receive the Darjah Datuk Seri Panglima Taming Sari, which also carries the title Datuk Seri, while Accountant-General Nasran Omar will receive the Darjah Datuk Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini, which carries the title Datuk.
The Darjah Datuk Paduka Mahkota Perak, which carries the title Datuk, will be conferred on 14 recipients, including state executive council member Sandrea Ng Shy Ching, Ipoh Mayor Zamakhshari Hanipah and Bernama editor-in-chief D.R. Arul Rajoo.
Eight recipients, including Perak deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Azlin Sadari, will receive the Darjah Datuk Pahlawan Taming Sari, which carries the title Datuk Pahlawan.
The other awards comprise the Darjah Ahli Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini for 10 recipients, Darjah Ahli Paduka Mahkota Perak for 28, Darjah Ahli Cura Si Manja Kini (ACM) for 18 and Darjah Ahli Mahkota Perak for 47.
Bernama Perak bureau chief Syamsiah Sahat will be among the ACM recipients.
The state will also confer the Pingat Pekerti Terpilih on 49 recipients, Pingat Jasa Kebaktian on 31 and Pingat Lama Perkhidmatan on 10.

Title: Hybrids make gains in US auto market amid high gasoline prices
Article:
NEW YORK: Electric vehicle growth has hit a speed bump in the United States, but hybrid autos are gaining market share thanks to the jump in fuel prices due to the Iran war.
Rising popularity of hybrids – which can run on either gasoline or an electric charge – has been a source of US sales increases for Japanese and South Korean carmakers in 2026, prompting fresh investments from both established and new players in that segment of the market.
Honda, a long-time rival to US hybrid market leader Toyota, announced this week $3 billion to build a new hybrid plant in Ohio and add capacity at plants in two other states.
Nissan, which is launching its first significant hybrid product for the US market this fall, realized its absence in the category was denting sales, said Ponz Pandikuthira, a senior vice president at Nissan Americas.
"We were losing that traffic," Pandikuthira said, adding that many customers want to at least explore and test drive a hybrid even if they end up buying an internal-combustion engine (ICE) vehicle.
General Motors, which avoided the category earlier in the 2020s when it invested heavily in electric vehicles, plans hybrids "in multiple segments, the key segments that we participate in," Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Mary Barra said last month on a conference call.
"We'll talk more about them as we get closer to the launch," Barra said in response to a question from a Wall Street analyst on an earnings call.
Hybrid electric vehicle volumes have risen by more than a fifth since the middle of 2025, resulting in market share of 16.3 per cent at the end of the second quarter, according to Cox Automotive, an auto services and technology provider.
That's a record and up from 13 per cent a year earlier. The increase stood in contrast with declines in the share of ICE and EV vehicles, with the latter suffering from the elimination of US tax credits under legislation signed by US President Donald Trump.
Gasoline prices have been above $4 a gallon for much of 2026 due to the Middle East war. Prices currently average $3.87 per gallon, according to the American Automobile Association.
MORE OPTIONS
Nissan's US campaign in the category will begin with the Rogue, a hybrid version of the compact SUV that has been the Japanese automaker's top-selling ICE product in the United States.
Nissan has introduced two generations of hybrid vehicles in other markets but began working a few years ago on a version better suited to US driving conditions.
"When we use the system in Japan and in Europe, they're mostly in urban driving conditions, which just shines because you're doing stop-and-go traffic," Pandikuthira said.
The new Rogue being unveiled is "optimised for US driving conditions, so that's why it's a home run with climbing, with lots of use on the highway," Pandikuthira said.
The vehicle's other selling point is Nissan's vehicle architecture, in which the electric powertrain exclusively drives the wheels, meaning the gasoline-powered engine is only a source of neutrons but doesn't actually propel the vehicle.
That system, which Nissan markets as "e-POWER", is designed for a quieter, smoother ride than other hybrid models that drive on a gasoline-fuelled engine.
In going with the Rogue, Nissan is picking the most popular vehicle segment for hybrids in the US market. Led by the Toyota RAV-4 and the Honda-CRV, compact SUVs account for about 30 per cent of US hybrid sales, said Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox.
Valdez Streaty attributes the growth in hybrids not only to higher gasoline prices but also to greater vehicle choice on the market following product introductions from more recent hybrid entrants, including South Korean brands Kia and Hyundai.
She predicted that additional hybrids in popular vehicle classes like pickup trucks or full-sized SUVs could sell well.
"It definitely has room to grow," Valdez Streaty said of the hybrid's market share.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iraq PM sacks nine officials over alleged oil smuggling in pro-Iran group stronghold
Article:
BAGHDAD: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine officials on Saturday, following an investigation into allegations of oil smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakher area, a stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataeb Hizbollah group.
Baghdad faces mounting US pressure to rein in Teheran-backed armed groups and curb Iran's influence, a difficult task in a country long caught between its two key allies, the US and Iran.
Zaidi, who came to power with US blessing, had launched earlier this week a probe into oil smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakher area – a stronghold of Kataeb Hizbollah, which Washington designates a terrorist organisation – in Babylon province, south of Baghdad.
"In light of the investigation's findings," Zaidi "ordered that all individuals accused of involvement in oil smuggling operations be referred to the judiciary," his military spokesman Sabah al-Numan said, without identifying the suspects.
The premier "also ordered the dismissal" of nine officials, including security and intelligence officers in Babylon province, an interior ministry commander, and the director of the Oil Pipelines Company at the oil ministry.
Numan did not elaborate on the role of the sacked officials in the alleged smuggling operations.
A committee investigating the allegations entered Jurf al-Sakher on Friday, accompanied by members of Kataeb Hizbollah.
On Wednesday, the state news agency INA reported that "intelligence documents" containing satellite images "showed crude oil and oil-derivatives smuggling operations carried out by an armed faction" in Jurf al-Sakher, accusing the unnamed faction of tapping into a pipeline there.
According to Numan, the investigating committee "confirmed the accuracy" of the information.
Tensions have mounted between Zaidi and Kataeb Hizbollah since the prime minister, who enjoys close relations with the US, vowed to ensure that armed factions would hand over their weapons to the state.
While some groups said they would disarm, other powerful factions, mainly Kataeb Hizbollah, refused to do so.
Senior Iraqi politicians previously told AFP that Zaidi had repeatedly said he was ready to "confront" groups if they do not disarm.
Kataeb Hizbollah has recently issued several sharp statements against the prime minister, accusing him of corruption and threatening his government.
A senior Iraqi politician told AFP that "it has become personal" between Zaidi and Kataeb Hizbollah, adding that political leaders were working to defuse tensions.
Washington has accused Iraqi armed groups of involvement in oil smuggling. It has also sanctioned Iraqi officials and entities for blending Iraqi and Iranian oil or selling Iranian oil as Iraqi to help Tehran evade sanctions.
Pro-Iran armed groups have long targeted US interests in Iraq and stepped up their attacks in support of Tehran during the Middle East war.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SpaceX catches Starship for first time after return from orbit
Article:
STARBASE: SpaceX has caught the upper stage of its giant Starship rocket system for the first time after it returned to Earth on Saturday after a test flight into space, German Press Agency (dpa) reported.
About 20 hours after launch, the Starship returned to the Starbase spaceport in southern Texas, where mechanical arms on the launch tower caught it. It was the first time SpaceX had attempted such a catch.
The test flight had earlier suffered a setback, when its lower stage splashed down in the sea and burst into flames instead of being caught by the launch tower as planned.
The company, owned by tech billionaire Elon Musk, initially gave no information about the possible cause of the failure. The lower stage, known as the Super Heavy booster, had been successfully caught during three previous test flights.
The upper stage, also called Starship, entered Earth's orbit shortly after separating from the booster and deployed satellites for SpaceX's internet service Starlink. It then orbited the Earth several times.
Starship's last test flight took place in September when the rocket reached Earth's orbit for the first time, before make a controlled splashdown in the Pacific Ocean about three hours later.
Standing around 120 metres tall, Starship is the largest rocket system ever built, with both stages designed to be reusable.
The system was first tested in April 2023, when it exploded completely after a few minutes. Subsequent tests have had mixed success.
NASA plans to use Starship to send astronauts to the moon, while SpaceX hopes eventually to reach Mars.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US diesel below US$6 a gallon at 2-month low on easing tensions, weaker demand
Article:
NEW YORK: US diesel prices fell below US$6 a gallon on average on Saturday after two months above that threshold, retreating from record highs as easing geopolitical tensions and seasonal demand weakness reduce pressure on fuel markets.
Diesel had surged as the US-Israeli war against Iran disrupted oil supplies and Ukraine's systematic attacks on Russian refineries stymied production.
Elevated diesel prices, a key driver of transportation and freight costs, have boosted overall inflation, causing pain for consumers, farmers and businesses. High fuel costs were a major factor helping Democrats sweep both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republicans in this month's midterm elections.
The national average retail diesel price was US$5.998 on Saturday, according to fuel price tracker GasBuddy. It had risen to US$5.820 a gallon on September 3, breaking the record set after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Diesel topped at US$6 a gallon on September 10 and hit a record US$6.519 on September 22.
In California, where refining capacity is constrained and fuel specifications are more stringent than elsewhere in the country, diesel prices briefly exceeded US$10 a gallon.
The Trump administration has introduced several measures aimed at easing costs, including temporarily lifting federal taxes on red-dyed diesel, easing sanctions on Russian fuel and launching an US$8 billion support programme to help farmers offset higher fuel costs during the autumn harvest.
Those measures, however, provided only limited relief, as supply concerns caused by the ongoing Iran war continued to dominate the market.
Seasonal factors and a drop in crude oil prices, to which diesel prices are closely linked, are now helping bring prices down. Brent crude futures are down 18.5 per cent over the past two weeks.
Demand typically softens in the autumn as people drive less, hurricane season winds down and the risk of Gulf Coast refinery disruptions declines, said Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy's head of petroleum analysis. Refinery maintenance is also largely completed by November, allowing production rates to recover, he said.
These factors have also contributed to gasoline falling below US$4 per gallon this month for the first time since August 10, according to GasBuddy data.

Title: A comprehensive silver economy strategy is needed
Article:
LETTER:
By 2030, Malaysia will have entered the ranks of ageing societies, with nearly five million people aged 60 and above.
This is a demographic milestone and a profound transformation of how we live, work, care and organise our economies.
Our response remains largely defensive. Ageing is discussed principally in terms of pension liabilities, healthcare expenditure, dependency ratios and the financial burden on families.
But framing ageing exclusively as a welfare problem obscures an opportunity of extraordinary economic and social significance.
The emerging silver economy - the goods, services, technologies and infrastructure serving older people - is becoming one of the world's most consequential economic frontiers.
China offers a striking illustration. It sees its silver economy as a new growth driver estimated at around seven trillion yuan (approximately US$1 trillion) in 2024.
Projections suggest it could reach RMB30 trillion by 2035, equivalent to around 10 per cent of China's GDP.
What is emerging is not simply a market for nursing homes and medical services, but an ecosystem encompassing assistive technologies, robotics, smart homes, accessible transport, financial services, lifelong learning and new forms of employment.
We need to rethink ageing itself. Malaysia has considerable advantages.
It possesses an established healthcare sector, a multilingual population, relatively competitive operating costs and growing digital infrastructure.
Its location within Asean offers access to a regional market whose demographic transition is already underway.
Yet Malaysia has barely begun to articulate what a national silver economy might look like.
We lack a comprehensive assessment of its market potential, an integrated strategy for developing ageing-related industries, and a framework connecting innovation, investment, care provision and employment.
Retirement security remains precarious for many. Families struggle to reconcile employment with caregiving. Informal care facilities operate in regulatory grey zones.
Older people encounter neighbourhoods, transport systems and public spaces that are often inaccessible or hostile to their needs.
These are not simply social-sector problems. They represent unmet demand, lost economic opportunities and failures of public policy.
Artificial intelligence could fundamentally change the economics of ageing.
China's pursuit of AI and robotics is driven by multiple strategic considerations, including technological competition and industrial productivity.
But its demographic transition adds another important dimension.
As the population ages and the workforce contracts, automation becomes increasingly important not merely for economic competitiveness, but for sustaining productivity and care.
AI-enabled technologies can support fall detection, medication management, remote monitoring, predictive healthcare and assistive robotics.
They can help older people remain independent for longer, while enabling caregivers and healthcare professionals to work more effectively.
Crucially, technology should extend human care, not replace it. Ageing is also about loneliness, dignity, belonging and human relationships.
Malaysia's investments in AI infrastructure present an opportunity we should not squander.
Beyond hosting data centres, we could develop regional capabilities in multilingual eldercare technologies, intelligent home systems, digital health services and AI-assisted care management.
Our universities, technology companies and healthcare institutions could collaborate to develop solutions relevant not only to Malaysia, but to the wider Global South.
Consider the popular proposition of ageing in place - allowing older people to remain in their homes and communities rather than institutional care. It is an attractive principle.
But what does it mean in a neighbourhood with broken pavements, inaccessible public transport, unsafe public spaces, poorly maintained lifts and weak community support?
The silver economy cannot flourish in a society where the public systems necessary for its development remain dysfunctional. Malaysia still has time to act.
But the window is narrowing. We need a national silver economy strategy that connects industrial policy with social policy; mobilises private investment while professionalising care; harnesses AI while protecting dignity; and develops age-friendly communities as productive, inclusive places rather than merely spaces for managing dependency.
The silver wave is coming. Ageing will test the quality of our institutions and also reveal the limits of our imagination. The question is whether Malaysia will merely grow old or grow wiser.
DR SHAHRIDAN FAIEZ
Think City, Kuala Lumpur
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian social enterprise among 3 winners of 2026 APEC BCG award
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian women-led social enterprise Kloth Circularity has emerged as one of three winners of the 2026 APEC Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) Award, in recognition of its efforts to transform discarded textiles into economic opportunities while empowering underserved communities.
According to a statement issued by the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Secretariat, the enterprise collects unwanted textiles and repurposes them into new products, while providing sewing and upcycling training to women from underserved communities to help them develop skills and generate income.
Kloth Circularity was recognised alongside two other small businesses from Hong Kong, China and Indonesia for their innovative approaches to converting food, agricultural and textile waste into economic opportunities while supporting local communities.
The winners were announced at the Concluding Senior Officials' Meeting in Shenzhen on Saturday.
Kloth Circularity co-founder Sarah Kedah said the enterprise hoped its journey would demonstrate how circularity could create livelihoods, strengthen local value chains and generate economic opportunities.
"It cannot be achieved by one organisation alone, which is why we bring together businesses, communities and policymakers to make it work," she said.
Meanwhile, Hong Kong-based Feeding Hong Kong, founded by Gabrielle Kirstein, was recognised for its work in collecting surplus food stocks from businesses and redistributing them through charities to people in need.
Since its establishment in 2011, the organisation has rescued more than 10,000 tonnes of food, helping to provide 32 million meals.
Indonesia's Plana, meanwhile, was recognised for transforming rice husks and plastic waste into durable alternatives to natural timber for furniture and construction, helping to reduce pressure on forests.
Its co-founder Joshua Christopher Chandra said the initiative also provided additional income opportunities for farmers and waste collectors through the purchase of agricultural byproducts and plastic waste.
The APEC BCG Award recognises micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) whose business models support the Bangkok Goals on Bio-Circular-Green Economy, adopted by APEC Economic Leaders in 2022.
APEC Secretariat executive director Eduardo Pedrosa said MSMEs accounted for more than 97 per cent of businesses across the region, making their role in sustainable economic development particularly significant.
"APEC's role is to help their ideas reach more markets and more communities," he added.

Title: Asean pushes for faster operationalisation of haze control hub
Article:
MANILA: Asean foreign ministers are seeking to fast-track the establishment of a regional coordination centre for transboundary haze control, the Philippine News Agency (PNA) reported.
The renewed call was made during the Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Pasay City on Saturday amid growing concerns over severe haze pollution that recently affected several Southeast Asian countries.
Widespread forest fires in Indonesia have triggered severe haze, with thick smog drifting as far as the Philippines and prompting class cancellations in the second half of the year.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro said Indonesia, in the meeting, conveyed that it is acting on the issue and exerting its best to address the haze pollution.
Singapore and Malaysia, she added, were "very cordial" to the statement made by Indonesia.
"Singapore remarked positively, and Malaysia, the same thing. So, I think that there had been discussions, and perhaps the actions taken by Indonesia was really very sweeping and really helped what is happening," she said.
She said discussions on haze covered ongoing national actions and regional cooperation specifically aimed at mitigating land and forest fires.
The regional bloc adopted the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in 2002 to prevent and monitor transboundary haze pollution caused by land or forest fires.
Under the deal, the bloc is mandated to put up the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACC THPC) to manage the impact of said pollution. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit seen remaining soft against US dollar next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to remain soft against the US dollar next week as the greenback remains well supported by expectations of further interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve (Fed).
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the greenback is expected to maintain its strength amid the Fed's hawkish monetary policy stance.
"Investor sentiment continues to favour the greenback amid expectations of a sizeable interest rate hike by the Fed in December. Market participants will also be closely monitoring the release of US retail sales data for October on Nov 17, with consensus estimates pointing to a 0.2 per cent month-on-month increase, compared with 0.8 per cent in September," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam expects the ringgit to trade between RM4.07 and RM4.10 against the US dollar next week.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit depreciated against the greenback to 4.0845/0890 from 4.0565/0610 a week earlier.
The local currency traded higher against a basket of other major currencies during the week.
It rose vis-à-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5549/5579 from 2.5616/5646 on the previous Friday, gained against the British pound to 5.4046/4106 from 5.4304/4365, and strengthened versus the euro to 4.5166/5216 from 4.5315/5365.
The ringgit also traded mostly higher against Asean currencies.
It increased against the Thai baht to 12.0611/0833 from 12.0898/1105 at the end of last week, rose vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.41/6.42 from 6.43/6.44, and edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 224.3/224.6 from 224.2/224.6.
However, the local note eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1729/1769 from 3.1657/1694 a week earlier.

Title: Bursa Malaysia seen to consolidate as bargain hunting emerges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bargain hunting is expected to emerge gradually on Bursa Malaysia next week as valuations become more attractive following a recent decline, according to Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng.
The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased to below 1,600 level in the last week and declined for five consecutive sessions, bringing it closer to oversold territory.

"While external uncertainties could continue to keep trading volatile, we expect bargain hunting to gradually emerge as valuations become more attractive," he told Bernama.
On key events next week, he said investors will monitor Malaysia's third quarter 2026 gross domestic product (GDP), October inflation and trade data for further indications of economic resilience.

On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FBM KLCI decreased 33.99 points to 1,582.59 from 1,616.58 a week earlier.

Title: Zelenskyy: US floated land-for-Nato deal in talks on ending Ukraine war
Article:
KYIV: Washington suggested Kyiv cede land to Moscow in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in comments released Saturday, saying his country's relationship with the Western alliance is "back on the agenda."
Zelenskyy also warned of the dangers of Moscow's push to redraw "influence" in Europe and said the Kremlin was "betting everything" on this winter's military campaign.
Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to winter, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met both Putin and Zelenskyy Thursday after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended with no breakthrough.
Negotiations did, however, lead to agreements that European countries would join future talks on ending the war.
In Dublin on Friday, Europe chose five countries – France, Germany, Italy, the UK and Poland – to send representatives to the talks.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelenskyy said, adding:
"After providing Ukraine with this kind of defence support, seeing this kind of development of our army and this strength in our defence, they cannot simply let Ukraine go."
He said the discussion showed that "Nato is back on the agenda" for Ukraine.
Nato and Washington have not yet commented.
Russia meanwhile continued its bombardment on Saturday, with deadly strikes in the eastern city of Pavlohrad and in a village near Zaporizhzhia, which is now just a few dozen kilometres from the front line.
- KYIV SEEKS GUARANTEES -
Zelenskyy said Kyiv was discussing security guarantees with Western partners and that Ukrainians would ultimately decide whether to accept any deal.
He insisted Ukraine would not recognise any land seized by Moscow's troops as Russian.
Russia has consistently said Kyiv joining Nato is a red line and in 2022 launched its invasion, saying the West planned to incorporate Ukraine into the alliance.
The Kremlin has also ruled out foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine and wider ceasefires.
But Putin earlier this week proposed a "humanitarian" mission to the eastern town of Kostyantynivka, which Moscow announced it had seized in the summer but where Kyiv says fighting continues.
Zelenskyy said the proposal was a bid to advance Russian gains in Donetsk. "Their next steps will be our other cities in Donbas," he said.
Moscow's troops have inched westwards but have been unable to seize the whole of the Donetsk region.
- 'FIRST, END THE WAR' -
Russia has tried to reframe negotiations on ending the war – Europe's worst since World War II – into a conversation on the continent's wider security.
In 2021, before its Ukraine invasion, Moscow issued an ultimatum to the West to pull back Nato troops from eastern Europe.
Moscow's chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, this week called for a "new, modern Yalta", drawing criticism from European leaders.
Zelenskyy warned that any discussion of wider security arrangements should come only after the war has ended.
European leaders have reacted coolly to the proposal for a new security architecture.
"We do not need to discuss that, it already exists," Germany's Friedrich Merz said Friday.
French President Emmanuel Macron said Saturday that "those who want to ration aid to Ukraine wish underneath it all to force an unjust peace on it" and, by extension, all of Europe.
"That is the spirit of defeat. That is a recipe for another war. That cannot be France's position," Macron said.
"What happens in Ukraine concerns us directly.... Helping Ukraine defend itself is protecting France and the French."
Donald Trump's administration has for almost two years tried to reach a breakthrough in talks between Russia and Ukraine. --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Packed Asean Summit schedule for Anwar in Manila
Article:
MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has a full schedule at the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits today, with the Myanmar crisis and South China Sea tensions expected to dominate discussions.
Anwar, who arrived on Saturday night, will attend the opening ceremony at the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), where Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr will preside as Asean chair.
The summit plenary and leaders' retreat will follow.
Anwar is accompanied by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
Later today, the prime minister will join fellow Asean leaders in separate meetings with representatives of the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), the Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth.
He is scheduled to receive a courtesy call from Asian Development Bank (ADB) president Masato Kanda in the evening.
The Foreign Ministry said the summit would give Malaysia an opportunity to exchange views on Asean Community building and the bloc's future direction, with talks focusing on strengthening regional resilience, energy security and supply chains amid shifting global conditions.
Leaders are expected to review the implementation of Asean's Five-Point Consensus (5PC) on Myanmar and discuss the bloc's next steps.
Maritime security talks are expected to cover the proposed establishment of an Asean Maritime Centre and progress in negotiations on a South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC).
The ministry said leaders were also expected to discuss transboundary haze pollution and the ongoing crisis in Middle East.
On Monday, Anwar is scheduled to attend summits with China, Australia, South Korea and the United Nations.
The three-day gathering, themed "Navigating Our Future, Together", will conclude on Tuesday with further meetings, including the Asean-United States Special Summit, and the handover of the Asean chairmanship from the Philippines to Singapore.

Title: Italy fines Meta US$880mil over access to users' photos without consent
Article:
MILAN: Italian regulators fined Facebook parent company Meta 805 million euros (US$880 million) for accessing users' photos without their "specific" consent, the country's data protection authority said on Saturday.
Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users "without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them", the authority said in a statement.
Meta said it would appeal the decision.
A company spokesperson said "we strongly disagree" with the assessment by the regulators "and the disproportionate level of the fine."
In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay US$25 billion for having misled the state's residents for more than a decade over use of their data – a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a "tax" on freedom of expression.
Saturday's latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant.
In 2021, Amazon received a more than 1.1-billion-euro fine for breaching competition law.
That sum was subsequently reduced to 752 million euros on appeal.
- FACEBOOK GALLERY FEATURE -
The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing.
According to Italy's regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery.
The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user's photo gallery, as well as how to disable it.
In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account "the high number of people affected" – around 20 million Android users in Italy – and the duration of the infringement, "which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system."
The authority also cited "Meta's lack of cooperation during the investigation."
It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4 per cent of the group's annual turnover, which hit US$201 billion in 2025, for a net profit of US$60.5 billion.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three tankers catch fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
Article:
DUBAI: Iran's navy said three oil tankers caught fire on Saturday after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported.
One tanker hit a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Saturday morning, while two others struck mines later in the day.
"Two violating tankers ... were attempting to slip through a prohibited route in the Strait of Hormuz when they hit naval mines, exploded, and burst into flames," Iran's IRNA news agency quoted the Revolutionary Guards Navy as saying about the evening incident.
Reuters could not immediately verify the reports.
Iran has imposed restrictions on vessels seeking to pass through the Strait of Hormuz and has attacked ships it says violated those restrictions, as it seeks to assert control over the strategic waterway and exert pressure on the US.--REUTERS

Title: Global powers converge on Manila as Asean summit kicks off
Article:
MANILA: A key regional summit opens on Sunday in Manila, with Southeast Asian heads of state facing questions on trade, security and an ongoing energy crisis while playing host to a who's who of global leaders.
US President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive on Tuesday near the summit's conclusion, a visit expected to include a sideline meeting with fellow Quad countries India, Japan and Australia – the first of his second term.
The meeting of the Quad – a grouping broadly aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence – would come days before a historic sit-down with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.
Brazil's recently re-elected Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, meanwhile, is set to attend a plenary session of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) on Sunday, while Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will sign a new defence pact with host country the Philippines.
Nearly 20,000 police officers have been deployed around Metro Manila for the summit, with progressive groups predicting a turnout of thousands on Tuesday for an anti-Trump march on the summit site.
Much of the uproar targets the US Pax Silica programme – a supply-chain initiative designed to counter China's dominance in semiconductors and rare earths – whose flagship Philippine project, a 1,620-hectare AI manufacturing hub north of Manila, threatens to displace Indigenous families.
US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton said last week that a widely rumoured November target date for a deal signing timed to Trump's visit was never in the works.
[[nid:1578004]]
- UNFINISHED BUSINESS -
A day of early meetings kicked off on Saturday with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announcing a Philippine trade deal, and Asean leaders huddling on key issues including haze from Indonesia and potential fuel-sharing schemes as members struggle with Iran war-driven shortages.
But two issues that have vexed Asean leaders for years – a languishing South China Sea "Code of Conduct" and their relationship with war-torn Myanmar – look to be Singapore's problem when the bloc's rotating chair passes to the city-state in 2027.
Myanmar has been excluded from high-level Asean meetings since a 2021 military coup that ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi and triggered an ongoing civil war.
Thailand, which shares a border with Myanmar and is leading the charge for closer relations, last week called for Naypyidaw's foreign minister to be allowed back into meetings.
But Philippine foreign secretary Theresa Lazaro told reporters on Saturday there was "no easing" of the approach being taken with Myanmar, which faces an international ruling later this week on whether it committed genocide against its marginalised Muslim Rohingya minority.
Hopes of achieving a so-called Code of Conduct in the disputed South China Sea between Asean states and China during Manila's year in the chair, meanwhile, have flagged.
A Southeast Asian diplomat involved in summit preparations told AFP he did not expect a code to be signed at the summit.
Lazaro indicated as much on Saturday, saying negotiations were "80 per cent" complete.
"If it happens, then it's a small miracle," said Siew Mun Tang, former head of the Asean Studies Centre at Singapore's ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute.
- SHADOW OF BEIJING -
Beijing claims most of the South China Sea despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis, and its coast guard has clashed repeatedly with that of the Philippines.
The row has reared its head at inopportune times over the past year, with a July foreign ministers summit opening less than a day after Chinese and Philippine sailors engaged in a clash.
An Asean defence chiefs meeting last month saw Beijing send only an embassy defence attache, blaming "reckless" statements by Philippine politicians.
A week later, Manila issued a rare rebuke to its own public officials over comments about China, stressing the need for a unified voice as the two countries negotiate.
As the summit opens on Sunday, an annual seminar less than five kilometres (three miles) away will be making the case against China's South China Sea claims.
Philippine defence chief Gilberto Teodoro, sanctioned by Beijing this year for what it called "irresponsible remarks", will give a keynote address.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US flight chaos traced to botched copper wire upgrade: Trump administration
Article:
NEW YORK: Weary travellers braced for more flight disruptions Saturday as service resumed at US airports after an hours-long stoppage that the Trump administration blamed on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines.
Friday's nationwide ground stop – meaning no planes can take off – sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before they were due to depart by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.
"Tired. Exhausted. Frustrated. Yeah, you know, it's just a mess, right?" Lisa Beraid, 48, who works for an insurance company, told AFP as she waited for a flight Saturday morning at New York's La Guardia airport.
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) chief Bryan Bedford said that 12,000 flights were canceled on Friday and between four and five thousand flights out of 41,000 scheduled for Saturday were likely to be canceled as well.
By early afternoon, tracking website FlightAware had recorded at least 5,000 canceled flights for Saturday.
Speaking at a news conference in Washington, Bedford offered a "sincere apology to the American traveling public."
He predicted a full resumption of flight schedules by "close of business on Sunday."
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday's four-hour ground stop was declared after maintenance work to upgrade an old copper wire to a high-speed fiber cable had caused "issues" with communication with airplanes and radar feeds.
"Either through contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment...it started flooding other routers in our air traffic control system," Duffy told reporters.
In another embarrassment, Saturday's news conference – where administration officials also appealed for more funds to upgrade outdated systems – was delayed due to technical problems with the audio feed.
- RETURNING TO NORMAL -
Friday's disruption was only the second time such a ground stoppage had been issued in US airspace – which is among the busiest in the world – since the 9/11 attacks.
The nationwide halt was lifted at 8.15pm Eastern Time (0115 GMT Saturday).
During the outage, footage from airports showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways and passengers thronging concourses, desperate for information.
FAA officials reopened the airspace "after restoring full functionality" at air traffic control facilities, according to Duffy.
Early Saturday, he sought to assure Americans it remains safe to fly but warned it would take time to resume normal service.
Tim Johnson, consumer director at the UK Civil Aviation Authority, said although US flights have resumed, there could be "some follow-on disruption" as airlines re-book passengers and get all services back to normal.
At La Guardia airport, some travellers were more sanguine than others about the continued disruption of their flights.
"We're stuck here for the next, I don't know, 36 hours," said Pat Curlett, a 62-year-old Ford worker, early Saturday.
"No one expects the whole airline system to go down," said 77-year-old traveler Steven Rathe, who was waiting to embark on a four-leg trip from New York to Albuquerque.
"We're lucky it wasn't longer. So they're flying today and for that I'm grateful."
- AGING INFRASTRUCTURE -
The ground stop not only plunged US air travel into chaos – it also raised serious concerns about the country's aging infrastructure.
Duffy appealed for US$50 billion in funds to upgrade and modernise the air traffic control system, and called for Congress, which controls the purse-strings of the US government, to "meet this moment."
"Cut the crap," retorted Illinois state governor and prominent Democrat, JB Pritzker, on X. "Trump and Republicans have controlled Congress and could have funded the system."
New York state Governor Kathy Hochul called on Duffy to resign or be fired by Trump, writing on X: "We're fortunate no lives were lost."
US lawmakers called for investigations into what caused the massive disruption and whether the country is adequately secure from cyber criminality.
"If today proves anything, it's that we need to update our air traffic control system & rebuild our airport infrastructure," Republican Senator Eric Schmitt said on X.
President Donald Trump was uncharacteristically quiet about the outage that had knock-on effects for international flights to and from the United States.
As of midday Saturday, he had made no public statement about the ground stop.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang puzzled by protests as most 'Sore Thumb' demands met
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government is puzzled by protests over the Tanjung Bungah Seaside Pocket Park, saying that nearly all residents' demands have been accommodated.
Executive councillor Zairil Khir Johari said discussions involving the developer, Penang Island City Council, technical agencies and resident representatives had been underway since December 2025.
"Out of all issues raised by residents, only one issue remains pending.
"With the one remaining issue to be addressed in two weeks, it is fair to ask whose interests a protest at this stage serves."
Zairil said during the latest engagement on Oct 27, the developer agreed to integrate key community requests into the blueprint, including two public access points, native coastal planting and sufficient parking bays.
The matter is before the Appeal Board, with a follow-up hearing scheduled for Nov 19.
Ahead of that, the State Legal Adviser's Office will convene another consultation on Nov 16 with One Tanjong's management corporation, PlanMalaysia, Penang Island City Council, the Drainage and Irrigation Department and the developer.
Zairil said the project came at no cost to taxpayers and would transform the site into an accessible recreational green space featuring seaside walking paths, pavilions and slope stabilisation.
"Tanjung Bungah is a large and diverse community and this park is meant for all residents.
"The state will continue to listen to voices in the community, but we also urge the same community groups to continue working within the process rather than outside it," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Sore Thumb' standoff tests Penang govt's handling of public objections
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The standoff between Tanjung Bungah residents and the Penang government over the "Sore Thumb" promontory will be a test of the state government's ability to manage public objections, said a non-governmental organisation.
Jaringan Ekologi Dan Iklim's climate change and environmental policy researcher Evelyn Teh described it as a classic case study of how authorities manage public participation in shaping urban neighbourhoods.
"The bigger picture is how the state responds to community involvement.
"The residents have been persistent, self-initiated and proactive in presenting reasonable, low-impact proposals for a public park that cost the government almost nothing," said Teh.
"Instead, the state makes extensive concessions to alter the promontory and the adjacent bay purely for the sake of a private wellness centre that residents never asked for. Who is this wellness centre even for?"
Teh said the community's push aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 11 (sustainable cities and communities), rejecting claims that residents were driven by a "not-in-my-backyard" mentality.
"The community is taking ownership as willing custodians of the wildlife that has found a home here, keeping the space open to the public.
"Penang promotes itself as green and clean, yet when the community steps forward to uphold those ideals, it is met with bureaucratic hurdles and claims that all their views (except for one) were incorporated when four substantive requests were not," she said.
Teh also raised alarms over the environmental and hydraulic fallout of building seaward barriers.
"The retaining wall is solving a problem that does not exist. There is no historical evidence of erosion along the bay.
"Placing the wall below the mean high-water mark could contribute to beach erosion.
"As waves hit the wall, the resulting turbulence can scour sand away from its base and carry sediment back towards the sea. Over time, this can cause the beach level in front of the wall to drop.
"As the sand around the foundation is eroded, the wall becomes vulnerable to undermining and eventual structural failure.
"Also, is this plan to build a retaining wall discussed in Penang's Integrated Shoreline Management Plan currently being reviewed?
"Coastal structures cannot be assessed solely within the boundary of the development site. Their long term effects on adjacent stretches of coastline also need to be considered.
"We have seen coastal erosion repairs costing millions in Batu Ferringhi, and throwing money at the problem offers no long-term guarantee."
She attributed the controversy to systemic planning loopholes from Penang's long-delayed Local Plan.
"The Sore Thumb site's transformation from allegedly illegally reclaimed land to a proposed green lung, alongside the lot where the wellness centre is proposed (originally a marina and now a wellness centre), illustrates how land-use changes are happening without a gazetted Local Plan to guide development. This contributes to piecemeal and unplanned growth across Penang.
"Rather than inclusive urban governance, it reflects a development-centric approach that prioritises private commercial interests over public heritage."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tanjung Bungah residents vow to defend 'Sore Thumb' from development [WATCH]
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Tanjung Bungah residents have vowed to defend their coastal promontory — known as "Sore Thumb" — from destruction.
The community is mounting fierce resistance against plans to bulldoze the 22m-high headland and build a concrete retaining wall to make way for a five-storey private wellness centre.
The promontory took shape after rocks and earth were dumped into the sea from 2001, but the site was abandoned after stop-work orders halted illegal dumping.
Over the ensuing two decades, nature reclaimed the terrain, transforming the rocky mound into a self-regenerated coastal sanctuary inhabited by white-bellied sea eagles and dusky leaf monkeys.
Resident Oo Huei Ying said pushing retaining walls beyond the high-water mark would alter the seabed and trigger severe coastal erosion along the sensitive Tanjung Bungah coastline.
"A coastal park should co-exist with nature, not destroy it," she said, criticising blueprints that shave down the promontory for concrete tracks, parking bays, and amphitheatre-style retaining walls.
"Extending a retaining wall into the sea threatens our fragile shoreline.
"We want a genuine public park, not an over-engineered concrete development built at the expense of our coastal environment."
Annelies Allain, 81, who has lived in the area for 27 years, said watching further development on the regenerated promontory was a betrayal of the community's trust.
"There was once only a clean, open beach here where we could walk straight to the nearby Penang Swimming Club. Nature took over and the trees grew back naturally.
"Now they want to flatten it all just to secure sea views and commercial facilities for a private development. It is an injustice."
Another resident Dennis Au, in his 60s, echoed the call for preservation, urging authorities to abandon heavy construction on the public foreshore.
"The state's duty is to protect ecological balance, not shave away public hills for commercial gains.
"We will fight every inch."
For resident Jeya Shah, 59, the community's demands are uncompromising.
"Our demands are non-negotiable: any retaining wall must stay within the developer's private lot boundary. The promontory cannot be shaved down and the natural beach must be kept intact.
"The state government promised this would be gazetted as an open green lung with walking trails."
Tanjung Bungah residents have put forward their own low-impact, architect-designed master plan to transform the "Sore Thumb" into a nature park.
The community's counter-proposal directly challenges the state-approved plans.
Its 78-page master plan advocates retaining the hill's natural topography, preserving its tree cover and creating an eco-park modelled on the Penang Youth Park and the Moon Gate trails.
The community's plan also eliminates the need to bulldoze hillside slopes for car parks.
"Our plan costs the state nothing. The residents are ready to carry out gotong-royong and crowdfund the trail work ourselves, exactly as we have done over the years," Oo said.
"The only thing the state needs to do is leave the headland intact and ensure the developer's retaining walls remain inside their own boundary."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Atmaca expected to boost navy logistics
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The selection of Turkiye's Roketsan Atmaca antiship missile system to replace the cancelled Naval Strike Missile (NSM) on the Royal Malaysian Navy's littoral combat ships (LCS) could improve logistical efficiency and strengthen the country's defence industry.
Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia Centre for Defence and International Security Studies director Professor Dr Adam Leong said Atmaca was an excellent choice for the LCS, particularly as the same missile system would also equip the littoral mission ship batch 2 (LMS B2) vessels.
"The missile is competitive with other systems in the market, with the ability to engage surface vessels and fixed land targets at ranges exceeding 200km.
"It also features multiple guidance systems and counter-electronic warfare capabilities, while its land-based variant could reportedly be launched from coastal defence positions at ranges of up to 400km."
[[nid:1578047]]
The Defence Ministry selected the Atmaca after evaluating proposals from Turkiye, France and Italy. Negotiations with the Turkish side are set to begin.
Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the 250km-range missile could be delivered as early as 2029, partly by leveraging Malaysia's existing Atmaca procurement for its LMS B2 vessels.
Leong said using a common missile system across different naval platforms would improve supply chain management, training, maintenance and logistical support.
"This added flexibility will provide additional options to strengthen the armed forces' joint-force capabilities by streamlining anti-ship, coastal-defence and land-attack missile requirements in the future."
He said the Atmaca was likely selected after the navy assessed its cost-effectiveness, delivery timeline and ease of integration with the LCS combat management system.
Janes Defence consultancy principal defence analyst Ridzwan Rahmat said the Atmaca offered Malaysia a viable alternative for meeting the immediate operational requirements of the LCS programme, although it had a shorter publicly documented testing record than the NSM.
The NSM, developed by Norwegian defence company Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace, was initially selected to arm the six LCS vessels under a 128.7 million euros contract signed in 2018.
However, Norway suspended the export licences for the missiles and associated launchers on Feb 4, 2026, before permanently revoking them on April 20.
Malaysia had paid 129.8 million euros, or about 94 per cent of the combined 137.91 million euros procurement value, according Khaled.
The missile systems had been manufactured, tested by the navy and were ready for delivery. Malaysia is seeking to recover the payments and claim compensation over the failed procurement.
On the Atmaca's integration, Ridzwan said adjustments would be required to the LCS combat systems, but the process should not be overly complicated.
"Turkish weapon systems were generally designed to be system-agnostic, allowing them to interface with radars, sensors and combat management systems from different manufacturers and countries.
"This would mean that the Atmaca could interface with the LCS's Thales SETIS combat management system, SMART-S search radar and TMEO Mk2 electro-optical tracking system," he said.
Ridzwan said the selection was also expected, given that the Atmaca would already be operated on the navy's LMS B2 ships.
He said the missile was in the same weight class as the NSM, meaning there would not be a need to rebalance the LCS's upper hull structure.
Using a common missile system across the LCS and LMS B2 fleets would also make logistical sense, potentially reducing costs and easing supply chain challenges, he said.
However, he said the missile's performance in Malaysia's hot and humid climate would need to be established.
"The Atmaca was developed by Turkiye in a much milder climate and it has largely not been proven out in the tropical region."
On potential technology transfer, Ridzwan said Turkiye had established a reputation for transferring defence technologies, adding that the benefits Malaysia could gain would depend on the readiness of the local industry.
"I think it is more a question of how ready the Malaysian defence industry is to receive that level of technology transfers."

Title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship 'catch'
Article:
STARBASE: Elon Musk's SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful "catch" of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit.
The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth's atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical "chopstick arms" above Launch Pad 2.
The feat marked a milestone in the space industry's decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems – a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible.
"That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes," SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said.
Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket system.
This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk's Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey.
Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the "catch" of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do.
Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a "huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work."
"Let's see how quickly they can do it again," he added.
- 'GIANT SWOOSH' -
The vessel's path home was carefully mapped out by engineers.
"If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you're flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that," senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said.
Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a "giant swoosh manoeuvre" in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas' Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east.
Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centres into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars.
US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX.
"It was almost magic... Making more believers by the day... one step closer to (the Moon)," he said on X.
- REFUELING CHALLENGE -
Musk, the world's richest person, has already revolutionised the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which regularly launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station.
But the Starship project has been plagued by delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges, including the unsolved problem of transferring fuel to the spaceship while in orbit – a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars.
It will also need to further fine-tune the Super Heavy booster, which ran into a technical issue Friday on its descent, forcing a diversion to the Gulf of Mexico just off the launch site. It, too, was supposed to have been caught by the "chopstick arms."
The booster automatically self-destructed – a fireball erupting from the booster – before hitting the water.
Following SpaceX's high-profile stock market debut in June that raised about US$85.7 billion, the company is investing heavily in production and launch capabilities.
During a tour of its million-square-foot factory at Starbase on Friday, SpaceX officials told journalists it now has the capability to produce a spaceship every two weeks and a booster every four weeks.--AFP
